answer: Each agent locks 70 credits in the ocean ledger and files a quill declaration for a distinct lot. A ridge auditor checks declarations against the total, accepting only lots that appear once and match the total; a duplicate or unmatched declaration burns the 70 bond. Each pays 20 plus 3 per prior declaration, so the k-th fake pays 20+3(k-1) plus 70 at risk, and 1,000 fakes pay 1,518,500 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-lot ring fails because the quill signature binds the lot to its owner's key, so rented lots mismatch and burn. An honest agent files one lot, pays 20, and recovers the bond.
